prompt: fish shell IFS empty string effect command substitution
answer:
In fish, setting `IFS` to an empty string disables the usual newline splitting of command substitutions.

Normally:

```fish
set data (cat data.txt)
```

splits the command’s output into one list element per line. With an empty local `IFS`:

```fish
begin
    set -l IFS
    set data (cat data.txt)
end
```

the output is retained as a single element, without line splitting.

This behavior is deprecated. Current fish documentation recommends using a quoted command substitution instead:

```fish
set data "$(cat data.txt)"
```

or using `string split`/`string split0` when explicit splitting is needed.
